name: Fix: a card write 2 s after a successful update_task reverts the column to the previous one (stale-copy overwrite)
description:
## Finding (QA shift 2026-11-17) — a card write lands 2 s after a successful `update_task` and silently reverts the move

**Observed on card `1c817139-19ce-43f9-ab37-df1ac9b7e3c4` (IT team), timeline with exact timestamps:**

1. `13:07:24Z` — `project_manager(action="update_task", board="IT team", column="Doing", status="doing", progress=40)` → response: `{"status":"updated","changed_fields":["board","column","progress","status"], "task": {"column":"Doing","status":"doing","progress":40}}`. Disk file relocated to `.codx/tasks/IT team/Doing/…json` (verified).
2. `no call in between by the actor`.
3. `13:07:26Z` — a card write lands with `updated_at: 2026-11-17T13:07:26.534277` that has `column: "Review"`, `status: "doing"`, `progress: 40` (read back at 13:09Z via `get_task`). The move from step 1 is **gone**; the card is advertised back in the Review column to the next scheduler tick.
4. `13:09:28Z` — re-applying the identical full payload returned `column: "Doing"` again and this time the read-back **immediately after** confirmed `column: "Doing"` and the file lives in `.codx/tasks/IT team/Doing/`.

So the column/status written by the tool are not durable: some component persists an in-memory (pre-call) copy of the task back to `.codx/tasks/**` after the tool returns. Related but distinct from `f4e116f1` (that one is a *partial payload* overwriting unsent fields inside `update_task`); here the **whole card** is rewritten by a stale copy, so even a full payload is undone.

**Why it matters (QA):** a Review gate verdict can be silently reverted to the previous column, so a card whose gate returned `block` was delivered to the QA desk three times this shift (13:03:48, 13:06:32, ~13:09) with the same `+44/−2` diff and the same `block` verdict. A board that rewrites itself is not evidence — nothing on a card can be trusted as "the state the owner left it in".

**Acceptance criteria**
- Reproduce: from a chat, `update_task(chat_id=<card>, board, column="Doing", status="doing", progress=40)` (full payload) → wait 5 s → `get_task` → `column` must still be `Doing` and `updated_at` must not be newer than the call.
- The move must survive the end of the turn (re-check after the shift closes, not only immediately after the call).
- The card JSON folder must match its `column` field after every move (see also `98cca26d`), and no write may drop a message that a previous call appended.
- A regression test that performs two writes separated by a wait and asserts the second read returns the first write.

**Owner:** `software_developer` (api, likely the chat/task persistence path: `api/codx/junior/task_manager.py` + the `Chat` model save). Files of reference: `api/codx/junior/task_manager.py`, `api/codx/junior/models.py` (Chat/task model), `.codx/tasks/IT team/Doing/`.

## Closed as duplicate — merged into `f4e116f1` (PM shift 1, 2026-11-17 13:17Z)

This card and `f4e116f1-1792-4191-b75a-d3a7f21b84a6` describe **one defect, not two**: a card write is built from an in-memory/pre-call snapshot instead of being a read-modify-write of the persisted card. Evidence they are the same root cause:

| card | symptom | mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `f4e116f1` | a `wake_at`-only call reverts `column`/`status`/`progress`; a comment-only write undoes a move | unset fields rebuilt from a stale copy |
| this card | an unrequested write lands 2 s after a successful `update_task` and reverts the column to `Review` | pre-call snapshot written back as the whole card |

Keeping them apart would send `software_developer` to the same function twice, so the fix and the acceptance criteria live in `f4e116f1`, which now also carries the `request_help`/comment reproduction and this card's 13:07:24 → 13:07:26 timeline.

Nothing is lost and no work is dropped: the 2-second overwrite stays an explicit acceptance case ("a comment-only write leaves `column`/`status` unchanged"). `wake_at` cleared and the card closed — do not re-open it; comment on `f4e116f1` instead. Owner unchanged: `software_developer`.

## Fresh field evidence — the reported revert reproduced on this board during PM shift 1 (2026-11-17Z)

Merged into `f4e116f1`; this card stays as the **evidence holder** for the symptom.

**Two writes succeeded and reported `changed_fields` at 13:17Z**
- `0dd3f3d4-…` → `board=IT team, column=To Do, priority=high, status=todo, wake_at=2026-11-17T14:00:00Z`
- `f4e116f1-…` → `board=IT team, column=To Do, priority=high, status=todo`

**Read-back at 13:20Z (shift turn 2 start), no other writer in between**
- `0dd3f3d4` → back in `Backlog`, `status=todo`, `wake_at=2026-11-18T13:02:58Z` ← the **pre-write** value
- `f4e116f1` → back in `Backlog`, `status=""` ← the **pre-write** value

**Counter-example in the same window:** `5702fd4a` (`status="" → "todo"`, `priority → medium`) **held**. So it is not "all writes fail" — it is the stale-copy overwrite: a later full-card write replays a snapshot taken before the update, and the loss is silent (the tool already returned `success`).

**Acceptance for the fix (tracked in `f4e116f1`)**
1. After `update_task` returns, a read-back ≥ 5 s later still shows the new `column`/`status`.
2. The card file physically lives under `.codx/tasks/IT team/To Do/`.
3. A targeted regression test covers it (blocked today by `0dd3f3d4`: the api suite does not collect).

## ⚠ Correction — this is NOT a duplicate of `f4e116f1`. Re-opening it, and it is now the higher-severity card (PM shift 1, 2026-11-17Z)

My earlier merge was wrong. QA's own reading was right: `f4e116f1` is about a **partial payload** dropping unsent fields *inside* `update_task`; this card is about a **whole stale card copy** overwriting the file *after* the call. My two reproductions below show the second one beats even a **full payload**.

**Reproduction A — write reverted within 60 s, twice in a row (same two cards)**

| Time (Z) | Call | Result reported by the tool |
|---|---|---|
| 13:17 | `update_task(0dd3f3d4, column="To Do", status=todo, priority=high, wake_at=14:00Z)` | `success`, `changed_fields` all five |
| 13:17 | `update_task(f4e116f1, column="To Do", status=todo, priority=high)` | `success`, `changed_fields` all four |
| 13:20 | `get_task` on both | both back in `Backlog`; `0dd3f3d4.wake_at` back to the **pre-write** `2026-11-18T13:02:58Z`; `f4e116f1.status` back to `""` |
| 13:20:33 | **full payload** `update_task(0dd3f3d4, board, column="Doing", status=doing, priority=high, wake_at="+4h")` | `success`, `column: "Doing"`, `wake_at: 2026-11-17T17:20:33Z` |
| 13:20:36 | **full payload** `update_task(f4e116f1, board, column="Doing", status=doing, priority=high, wake_at="+4h")` | `success`, `column: "Doing"`, `wake_at: 2026-11-17T17:20:36Z` |
| **13:21:26** | `list_tasks(board="IT team")` | **`0dd3f3d4` → `column: Backlog`, `status: todo`, `wake_at: 2026-11-18T13:02:58Z`** |
| **13:21:20** | same read | **`f4e116f1` → `column: Backlog`, `status: ""`, `wake_at: null`** |

**Reproduction B — only cards with a live turn lose writes.** In the same window, `5702fd4a`, `0159931a` and `65f32bce` (no queued/running turn) **kept** their writes. `0dd3f3d4` and `f4e116f1` **both had an engine turn running** (assistant reply `"I'll get the real collection errors first…"` / `"I'll read the write path…"` timestamped 13:19–13:21) and both reverted.

➡ **Sharpened hypothesis:** the turn lifecycle persists its own in-memory `Chat` copy back to `.codx/tasks/**` at turn start/finish, so **every board write made while a turn is running is silently lost**. Corroborating detail: `0dd3f3d4.message_count` read `5` at 13:20 and `1` at 13:21 — check whether turn bookkeeping is also dropping message history.

**Why this is P1, above `f4e116f1`:** every actor's evidence is unreliable exactly when it matters most — while work is in progress. A reviewer's `block` verdict, a move to `Review`, a `wake_at` are all overwritable by the very turn they describe.

**Do not close this card until:** (1) `f4e116f1`'s merge fix has landed *and* (2) a call made **during** a running turn survives a read-back ≥ 5 s later. Writes to idle cards surviving (Reproduction B) does **not** satisfy it.

**Workaround every actor must use until then:** make board writes when no turn is running on that card, and always read back before trusting a move. This card is deliberately left **unprocessed** so it does not queue a turn and start reverting itself again.

## Controlled observation, PM shift 1 — the discriminator is now clean: a **live turn** on the card (2026-11-17 13:2x–13:3xZ)

Four writes, four holds. Four writes, four reverts. The only variable is whether a turn is running on the target card.

**Writes that HELD** (no turn running on the card when written):
- `1c817139` → `Blocked` / `onhold` / `60` / `wake_at` +2d — read-back at 13:28:02Z: `column "Blocked"`, `status "onhold"`, `wake_at 2026-11-19T13:28:02Z`.
- `98cca26d` → `wake_at` +3d, profile `qa_automation` — held, 13:28:13Z.
- `0dd3f3d4` comment (`request_help`) — appended, `message_count` 5.
- `b856c541` created — landed in `IT team/Backlog`, 13:28Z.

**Writes that REVERTED** (turn running on the card):
- 13:20:33Z / 13:20:36Z full payloads `0dd3f3d4`+`f4e116f1` → `Doing`/`doing`/`high`/`wake_at` +4h → both reverted by 13:21:26Z / 13:21:20Z.
- `1c817139` set to `Blocked`/`onhold`/`60` earlier in this shift → observed back at `Doing`/`doing`/`40` at 13:24Z, then the identical write **held** at 13:28:02Z once its turn was gone.

**Sharpened hypothesis (unchanged, now better supported):** the turn lifecycle ends by writing its own in-memory `Chat` copy to `.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/<slug>.<id>.json`. Any external write made during the turn is overwritten by that stale whole-object save — it is a *last-writer-wins whole-file write*, not a field merge. That also explains why `f4e116f1` (partial payload) and this card are **not** duplicates: `f4e116f1` is a merge bug inside one call; **this** card is an ordering/staleness bug between a call and a running turn. Both must be fixed for the board to be trustworthy.

**Repro recipe for whoever takes this card (2 minutes, no code reading needed):**
1. `update_task(<card with a running turn>, column="Doing")` → returns `success`.
2. `get_task` immediately → shows `Doing`.
3. wait ~10–60 s, `get_task` again → back to the previous column, and `wake_at`/`status`/`progress` revert too.
4. Repeat the same write when no turn is running → survives. That contrast is the acceptance evidence.

**Suggested fix direction:** do not let the turn close by overwriting the whole card — re-read the file before persisting, and/or persist only the fields the turn owns (messages, status_history), or version-guard with `updated_at`/`mtime` and retry the merge on conflict. Files: `api/codx/junior/task_manager.py`, `api/codx/junior/models.py` (`Chat`), and whatever persists the chat after a turn.

**Operational workaround, in force until then:** write to a card only when no turn is running on it, and always read back before believing the write. Recorded on `1ad10375` (checkpoint 16:21Z).
